candidates.name: Cutaneous Cryptococcosis
support_spans: A 62-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis treated with fingolimod for 3 years presented with a tender nodule on her forehead, which had gradually grown over 3 weeks.
Skin biopsy: Granulomatous inflammation composed of histiocytes, giant cells, and lymphocytes admixed with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules
candidates.why: The patient presents with a tender nodule on her forehead and the skin biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules, consistent with Cutaneous Cryptococcosis.

candidates.name: Cryptococcal Cellulitis
support_spans: Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of an eroded, crusted papule on the forehead is consistent with Cryptococcal Cellulitis.

candidates.name: Sporotrichosis
support_spans: She reported bumping her forehead on an air-conditioning unit several months prior
candidates.why: The patient's history of trauma to the forehead and the presence of a tender nodule could be consistent with Sporotrichosis, although it is less likely given the biopsy results.

candidates.name: Blastomycosis
